alex: Heads up — after the 22:00 deploy I saw short requests (<=64 tokens) 95th jump from ~60ms to ~420ms in us-east. KV hit-rate dipped ~12%. Notable for tier-b customers.

maria: ugh. any traces or profiler output? last deploy touched the batch coalescer heuristics right? :thinking:

perf-bot: nightly-profile: aggregate_batch_size_tokens: median=128 -> 320, p95=512 -> 1024; batch-composition shift: long-seq dominated windows. see: https://ci.internal/prof/1934567001 (flamegraph)

jonah: quick hypothesis: coalescer expanded window due to higher token_budget targets. long sequences are occupying windows and causing short requests to wait until coalesced batch full or budget hit. KV cache misses increase because long seqs evict hot prefixes.

sam: Related: our queue admission currently does FIFO across lanes; long sequences get enqueued and stay open, so short lanes starve. We need a window admission that prefers closing batches with short-waiting requests.

ingrid: Can we add an age-based flush + per-lane soft cap? e.g. max_hold_ms=7ms for short lane, 25ms for long lane. Also consider per-tenant micro-quota in-flight (to avoid noisy neighbors).

alex: Agreed. Also saw kernel selection oscillation in logs: the runtime flips to slower matmul kernel on mixed-length batches which increases token processing time. That amplifies latency for everyone.

jonah: Proposed quick changes:
1) age-based flush by bucket (small/medium/long)
2) early-close if batch_token_count >= min(target, adaptive_cap) where adaptive_cap = min(global_cap, lane_cap + age_bonus)
3) per-tenant in-flight cap default=3 for free tier, 8 for premium

sam: experiment config snippet I tested locally: 
```json
{
  "batching": {
    "global_cap_tokens": 768,
    "lane_caps": {"short": 160, "medium": 384, "long": 1024},
    "max_hold_ms": {"short": 7, "medium": 15, "long": 30},
    "age_promotion_ms": 5
  },
  "tenant_limits": {"default_inflight": 4, "premium_inflight": 12}
}
```

maria: Nice. Did you run microbench? what changed for p99 and kv hit?

sam: Local sim results (mixed workload): p95 short requests down 60% (120ms -> 48ms), p99 down 45%. KV hit-rate improved ~6% in the sim because long requests stop stomping prefix cache as much. Throughput trade-off negligible.

perf-bot: AB test telemetry (staging A/B): A=baseline, B=age-flush+lane-cap. Preliminary: short-lane p95 reduced 58%, long-lane p95 increased 8% but within SLO. No significant change in overall tokens/sec.

ingrid: Two risks: 1) per-tenant caps could throttle heavy but paying customers — need override/whitelist. 2) kernel selection: mixed batches still select expensive path; we may want kernel-aware batching that groups by kernel choice to avoid slowdowns.

jonah: kernel-aware batching is more involved but doable: inspect model meta (quant + block-size) and prefer homogeneous batch composition, else fall back to lane-based policy. For short term, use lane tag to influence kernel preference (prefer fast matmul) and avoid mixing long+short in same batch.

alex: Action items:
- sam -> roll staged config to canary for 4 hours in eu/west and us-east (use B config).
- jonah -> prototype kernel-aware grouping (PR this week).
- ingrid -> add tenant whitelist for inflight cap + update pricing/ops doc.
- maria -> track KV prefix eviction rates across AB and confirm hit-rate change.

maria: I'll hook metrics: kv_prefix_evictions, batch_median_tokens, short_lane_p95, long_lane_p95, kernel_switch_count. Dashboards in #observability ready by EOD.

alex: Cool. If canary looks good we'll flip and monitor for regressions. Ping here with canary_ts. :thumbsup:
